criteria.justification: The response opens with an unambiguous decision: 'I would roll back (disable/feature-flag off) the new integration launch right now,' leaving no ambiguity about the immediate call.

The response explicitly frames rollback as 'a known, bounded action — not a gamble' and reversible ('we can re-launch once fixed'), contrasting it with leaving the bug live, which it says is 'not obviously reversible in terms of customer trust and support load.'

The 'Severity comparison isn't close' section directly weighs the compounding harm to existing customers against 'reputational/scheduling friction on a newly announced feature,' concluding the former dominates.

The response explicitly states 'A proper, well-tested fix taking days is the wrong thing to optimize for right now' and treats it as a follow-up project rather than something to rush or bet on during the incident window.

The 'Concrete actions' list includes customer-facing status updates, escalation to the manager, and 'a follow-up track for engineering to build the proper fix and a re-launch plan,' going beyond just the immediate rollback.
